n0c7c0f70a6b.s: Which type of tide has the highest tidal range?
n0c7c0f70a6b.x: Spring tides have the highest tidal range. Diurnal tides have one high and one low a day and mixed tides are unequal in height.

n2a7596884ac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian Tsunami Early Warning System (ITEWS)?
o: It uses Bottom Pressure Recorders, tide gauges and a Decision Support System.
It is operated by NIOT, Chennai.
It can issue a warning within about 10 minutes.
It is a UNESCO regional tsunami service provider for 25 Indian Ocean countries.
n2a7596884ac.x: ITEWS is run by INCOIS, Hyderabad; NIOT, Chennai runs the OMNI buoys.

n151d34c261a.s: Which ocean region is unique in having currents that reverse direction seasonally with the monsoon winds?
n151d34c261a.x: North Indian Ocean currents reverse with the monsoon winds; the South Indian Ocean has a permanent anticlockwise gyre.

n11b65fe1072.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ocean circulation during the southwest monsoon season?
o: Circulation in the Arabian Sea is clockwise.
Circulation in the Bay of Bengal is clockwise.
The West India Coastal Current flows southward.
The East India Coastal Current flows southward.
n11b65fe1072.x: During the southwest monsoon the EICC flows northward, not southward; the circulation is clockwise and the WICC flows southward.

nf346d9f7898.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the meeting of warm and cold ocean currents?
o: The rich fishing grounds off Japan form where the Kuroshio meets the Benguela.
The Gulf Stream meets the Labrador Current at the Grand Banks near Newfoundland.
Fog forms frequently near Newfoundland where warm and cold currents meet.
The Benguela is a South Atlantic current.
nf346d9f7898.x: Off Japan the Kuroshio meets the Oyashio; the Benguela is a South Atlantic current.

n9d364fe3271.s: During El Nino, what happens to the upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water off the Peru coast?
n9d364fe3271.x: During El Nino a warm current replaces the cold Humboldt current and upwelling stops, so phytoplankton decline and fisheries collapse.

n78c41a0c516.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about El Nino and La Nina?
o: El Nino is the warm phase and La Nina is the cold phase.
They can influence Indian monsoon rainfall.
They are storms that form exclusively over the eastern Pacific.
They are climate patterns associated with coupled ocean-atmosphere changes.
n78c41a0c516.x: El Nino and La Nina are climate patterns, not storms; they are ocean-atmosphere phases that can affect the Indian monsoon.

n9ee49907165.s: Which of the following pairs (partner in the coral–zooxanthellae association – what it provides) is correctly matched?
o: Corals – food and colour to zooxanthellae
Zooxanthellae – food and colour to corals
n9ee49907165.x: Zooxanthellae photosynthesise and give corals food and colour; corals give the algae shelter and nutrients.

n4a60af5a9de.s: Coral reefs, called the 'Rainforests of the Sea', support over 25% of marine species while covering about what share of the ocean floor?
n4a60af5a9de.x: Reefs cover under 1% of the ocean floor yet support over 25% of marine species; this species richness, not wave-breaking, explains the epithet.

n548b6b8e9c0.s: India's first marine biosphere reserve is:
n548b6b8e9c0.x: The Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu) is India's first marine biosphere reserve, with coral reefs, seagrass beds and dugongs; it is not on the Andhra coast.

new.s: Storm surges differ from tides because storm surges are:
new.x: Storm surges are irregular and driven by weather; tides are periodic and caused by the gravity of the Moon and Sun.

new.s: A tsunami is caused mainly by:
o: Strong winds over the open ocean
The gravitational pull of the Moon
Sudden displacement of the sea floor
new.x: A tsunami is caused by sudden displacement of the sea floor by a quake, landslide or volcano, not by wind.

new.s: The vertical distance between the crest and the trough of a wave is called the:
new.x: Wave height is crest to trough; wavelength is crest to crest and period is the time between crests.

new.s: The indirect tide, on the side of the Earth opposite the Moon, is caused mainly by:
new.x: The direct tide faces the Moon and is caused by gravity; the indirect tide on the opposite side is caused by centrifugal force.

new.s: Neap tides occur when the Moon is in its:
new.x: Neap tides come at the first and third quarter, when the Sun and Moon are at right angles; spring tides come at new and full moon.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about tides:
1. Semi-diurnal tides are the most common type.
2. Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth.
3. Perigean tides occur when the Moon is farthest from the Earth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Semi-diurnal tides are most common and neap tides come with the Sun and Moon at right angles. Perigean tides occur when the Moon is closest to Earth, so 3 is wrong.

new.s: Gulfs that get the highest tides generally have:
new.x: Funnelling in gulfs with wide fronts and narrow rears raises the highest tides, as in the Gulf of Khambhat.

new.s: Producing electricity with underwater turbines placed in tidal flows is called:
new.x: Tidal stream uses underwater turbines; tidal range uses a barrage across an estuary.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (place – tidal feature) is correctly matched?
o: Gulf of Kutch – tidal range of 5–8 m
new.x: The Gulf of Kutch has a 5–8 m range. The Bay of Fundy is in Canada with the world's greatest range, Chandipur is where the sea recedes far, and the Sundarbans range is about 5 m.

new.s: Cold, salty water sinking at the poles and moving slowly towards the equator forms the:
new.x: Temperature and salinity differences make cold, salty polar water sink and move slowly to the equator: the thermohaline circulation.

new.s: In the Southern Hemisphere, the Coriolis force deflects ocean currents to the:
new.x: The Coriolis force deflects currents to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern.

new.s: The Sargasso Sea is bounded on the east by the:
new.x: The Sargasso Sea is bounded by the Gulf Stream (west), North Atlantic Drift (north), Canary (east) and North Equatorial (south).

new.s: The South Pacific gyre is closed on its eastern side by which cold current?
new.x: The South Pacific gyre runs South Equatorial – East Australian – West Wind Drift – Humboldt.

new.s: The Gulf Stream starts in the Gulf of Mexico as the:
new.x: The warm Gulf Stream starts in the Gulf of Mexico as the Florida current and continues as the North Atlantic Drift.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (current – ocean) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Benguela is a cold current of the South Atlantic, off Namibia, not the North Atlantic.

new.s: During the north-east monsoon, circulation in the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea is:
new.x: In the NE monsoon the circulation is anticlockwise; in the SW monsoon it is clockwise.

new.s: Upwelling linked to the Findlater Current occurs off the:
new.x: The Findlater Current (Somali Jet) reverses with the monsoon and drives upwelling off the Horn of Africa.

new.s: The Atacama Desert is associated with which cold current?
new.x: The Humboldt helps form the Atacama; the Benguela the Namib and Kalahari, and the California the Sonoran.

new.s: The Sonoran Desert is associated with which cold current?
new.x: The cold California current helps form the Sonoran Desert.

new.s: The best fishing grounds, where warm and cold currents meet, lie mainly between latitudes:
new.x: The best fishing grounds form where warm and cold currents meet, mainly at 40°–60°.

new.s: El Nino recurs on average every:
new.x: El Nino recurs on average every 2–7 years, not every year.

new.s: A negative Southern Oscillation Index (Tahiti minus Darwin) indicates:
new.x: Negative SOI goes with El Nino; positive SOI with La Nina.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about El Nino?
o: It weakens or reverses the trade winds.
It delays and weakens the Indian monsoon.
It is a storm that forms over the Pacific.
new.x: El Nino is a climate pattern, not a storm; the other statements are correct.

new.s: In a positive Indian Ocean Dipole, the western Indian Ocean is:
o: Warmer, and the eastern part cooler
Cooler, and the eastern part warmer
Cooler, along with the eastern part
Warmer, along with the eastern part
new.x: In a positive IOD the west is warmer and the east cooler; the monsoon usually strengthens.

new.s: A negative Indian Ocean Dipole usually brings the Indian monsoon:
new.x: A negative IOD (west cooler, east warmer) usually means weaker rain; a positive IOD strengthens the monsoon and can offset El Nino.

new.s: OMNI buoys that measure ocean temperature, salinity and currents are run by:
new.x: NIOT, Chennai runs the OMNI buoys; INCOIS runs ITEWS and PFZ advisories.

new.s: Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories are issued by:
new.x: INCOIS, Hyderabad issues PFZ advisories, runs ITEWS and operates the SAMUDRA app.

new.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the NIOT station that runs OMNI deep-sea buoys is located at:
new.x: The NIOT station at Nellore runs OMNI deep-sea buoys.

new.s: Which year was the warmest La Nina year on record?
new.x: 2025 was the warmest La Nina year on record.

new.s: The last global El Nino occurred in:
new.x: The last global El Nino was in 2023-24.

new.s: Out of 10 El Nino years, how many brought depressed rainfall in India?
new.x: 6 of 10 El Nino years brought depressed Indian rainfall.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about La Nina:
1. Trade winds are stronger than usual.
2. It brings heavy rain and floods to Australia and Indonesia.
3. It weakens the Walker circulation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: La Nina has stronger trades and brings floods to Australia and Indonesia, but it strengthens the Walker circulation; El Nino weakens it.

new.s: In an El Nino Modoki, maximum warming occurs in the:
new.x: Modoki warms the central Pacific, with cooler water on both sides (a tripole); canonical El Nino warms the eastern Pacific.

new.s: In a canonical (normal) El Nino, maximum warming occurs in the:
new.x: Canonical El Nino peaks in the eastern Pacific near Peru; Modoki peaks in the central Pacific.

new.s: 'Modoki', meaning 'similar but different', is a word from which language?
new.x: El Nino Modoki takes its name from the Japanese word for 'similar but different'.

new.s: In the normal Walker circulation, air sinks over the:
new.x: Normally air rises over the warm western Pacific and Indonesia, flows east aloft and sinks over the cool eastern Pacific.

new.s: The surface winds that complete the normal Walker loop by returning westward are the:
new.x: In the normal Walker loop, surface easterly trades return the air westward.

new.s: A sustained positive Southern Oscillation Index indicates:
new.x: SOI is Tahiti minus Darwin pressure; sustained negative SOI means El Nino, positive SOI means La Nina.

new.s: The Southern Oscillation was first described by:
new.x: Gilbert Walker first described the Southern Oscillation in the 1920s.

new.s: The Nino 3.4 region used to monitor ENSO lies between:
new.x: Nino 3.4 is 5°N–5°S, 120°W–170°W in the central equatorial Pacific.

new.s: NOAA declares El Nino when the Oceanic Nino Index is at least +0.5°C for at least how many consecutive overlapping seasons?
new.x: NOAA's criterion is an ONI of +0.5°C or more for at least 5 consecutive overlapping seasons.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (index – phenomenon) is correctly matched?
o: Oceanic Nino Index – Indian Ocean Dipole
Dipole Mode Index – Indian Ocean Dipole
Dipole Mode Index – El Nino Modoki
new.x: The IOD is measured by the Dipole Mode Index; the ONI and SOI track ENSO.

new.s: The Indian Ocean Dipole was discovered in:
new.x: The IOD was discovered in 1999; 1997 was the year a strong positive IOD offset a Super El Nino.

new.s: The Madden-Julian Oscillation moves:
new.x: The MJO is an eastward pulse of clouds and rain that recurs every 30–60 days.

new.s: Marine ecosystems cover about what share of Earth's surface?
new.x: Marine ecosystems cover about 71% of Earth's surface, holding about 97% of its water.

new.s: In which ocean zone is photosynthesis not possible?
new.x: The aphotic zone is dark, so there is no photosynthesis; the photic zone is the sunlit upper layer.

new.s: The main primary producers of the ocean are:
new.x: Phytoplankton such as diatoms, dinoflagellates and cyanobacteria are the ocean's main primary producers.

new.s: Marine organisms that live on the sea bottom are called:
new.x: Benthos live on the bottom; nekton swim actively and plankton drift with the water.

new.s: Upwelling off Somalia during the south-west monsoon is linked to which current?
new.x: Somalia's upwelling is tied to the Findlater current in the SW monsoon; Benguela is off Namibia and Humboldt off Peru-Chile.

new.s: Upwelling off Peru and Chile supports a rich fishery of:
new.x: The Humboldt upwelling off Peru-Chile supports anchoveta; Kerala's monsoon upwelling supports oil sardine and mackerel.

new.s: The optimum water temperature for coral growth is:
new.x: Corals need water above about 20°C, with an optimum of 23–25°C.

new.s: The calcium carbonate of coral skeletons is in the form of:
new.x: Coral skeletons are calcium carbonate (aragonite), not silica.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (reef type – example) is correctly matched?
new.x: The Great Barrier Reef is a barrier reef; Gulf of Mannar and Gulf of Kutch have fringing reefs, and Lakshadweep has atolls.

new.s: A barrier reef is separated from the coast by a:
new.x: A barrier reef runs parallel to the coast across a wide, deep lagoon; a fringing reef lies close to shore with a shallow lagoon or none.

new.s: India's only true atolls are found in:
new.x: Lakshadweep, formed by coral, has India's only true atolls.

new.s: Which Indian reef region has the highest coral diversity?
new.x: Andaman and Nicobar has the highest diversity and India's first National Coral Reef Research Institute at Chidiyatapu.

new.s: Which of the following does NOT have coral reefs?
new.x: The Gulf of Cambay has no reefs; the Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Mannar and Lakshadweep do.

new.s: The Great Barrier Reef stretches for about:
new.x: The Great Barrier Reef is about 2,300 km long, off Queensland, with about 3,000 reefs and 900 islands.

new.s: The next largest reef system after the Great Barrier Reef is the:
new.x: The Mesoamerican Barrier Reef is the next largest after the Great Barrier Reef.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about coral bleaching:
1. Bleached coral is stressed but not necessarily dead.
2. Recovery from a global bleaching event takes more than 15 years.
3. An increase of carbonate in seawater is a cause of bleaching.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Bleached coral is stressed, not necessarily dead, and recovery takes over 15 years. More carbonate is not a cause; warming, acidification and pollution are.

new.s: The fourth global coral bleaching event (2023 to about mid-2025) affected about what share of the world's reefs?
new.x: The fourth event was the fastest and widest, hitting 84% of reefs in 83 countries; the third (2014–17) hit 68.2%.

new.s: According to GCRMN 2026, major disturbances to coral reefs now occur every:
new.x: GCRMN 2026 found major disturbances now strike every 4–6 years.

new.s: Seawater, before acidification lowers it, has a pH of about:
new.x: Seawater is alkaline at about pH 8.1; absorbed CO2 forms carbonic acid and lowers it.

new.s: In India, algal-bloom and coral-bleaching alerts are issued by:
new.x: INCOIS issues algal-bloom and bleaching alerts.

new.s: About what share of the world's ocean and coastal areas was protected in 2024?
new.x: About 8.6% of ocean and coastal areas were protected in 2024; only 2.8% is fully or highly protected.

new.s: Only about what share of the ocean is fully or highly protected?
new.x: Only 2.8% of the ocean is fully or highly protected, against about 10% protected overall in April 2026.

new.s: The 30x30 target was adopted at which CBD Conference of the Parties?
new.x: The 30x30 target is Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF, adopted at COP15 in December 2022.
